'''Hindustan Petroleum Corporation Limited''' ('''HPCL''') is an Indian [[public sector undertaking]] in [[Petroleum industry|petroleum]] and [[natural gas]] industry, headquartered in [[Mumbai]]. It is a [[subsidiary]] of the [[Oil and Natural Gas Corporation]] (ONGC), which is owned by the [[Government of India]] and under the administration of [[Ministry of Petroleum and Natural Gas]].<ref name="trendlyne.com">{{Cite web|title=Latest Shareholding Pattern - Hindustan Petroleum Corporation Ltd.|url=https://trendlyne.com/equity/share-holding/556/HINDPETRO/latest/hindustan-petroleum-corporation-ltd/|access-date=2020-07-29|website=trendlyne.com}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|date=2014|title=Sustainability report 2013-14|url=http://www.hindustanpetroleum.com/documents/pdf/HPCL_Sustainability_report_2014.pdf|url-status=live|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150317142817/http://hindustanpetroleum.com/documents/pdf/HPCL_Sustainability_report_2014.pdf|archive-date=17 March 2015|access-date=13 May 2015|page=7}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|title=List of Maharatna, Navratna and Miniratna CPSEs ||url=http://dpe.nic.in/publications/list_of_maharatna_navratna-and_miniratna|url-status=dead|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20130719123802/http://dpe.nic.in/publications/list_of_maharatna_navratna-and_miniratna|archive-date=19 July 2013|access-date=2013-07-28|df=dmy-all}}</ref>

Since 2018, Oil and Natural Gas Corporation has owned majority of its stake.<ref name="economictimes.indiatimes.com2">{{cite news|title=ONGC buys govt's entire 51.11% stake in HPCL for Rs 36,915 crore|newspaper=The Economic Times|url=https://economictimes.indiatimes.com/industry/energy/oil-gas/ongc-buys-govts-entire-51-11-stake-in-hpcl-for-rs-36915-crore/articleshow/62729805.cms|url-status=live|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180618175430/https://economictimes.indiatimes.com/industry/energy/oil-gas/ongc-buys-govts-entire-51-11-stake-in-hpcl-for-rs-36915-crore/articleshow/62729805.cms|archive-date=18 June 2018|access-date=10 October 2018}}</ref> It is ranked 367th on the ''[[Fortune Global 500]]'' list of the world's biggest corporations as of 2016.<ref>{{cite news|title=Fortune Global 500 list|work=CNN Money|url=http://beta.fortune.com/global500/list/filtered?hqcountry=India|url-status=live|access-date=22 July 2016|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160821170013/http://beta.fortune.com/global500/list/filtered?hqcountry=India|archive-date=21 August 2016}}</ref> On 24 October 2019, it became a [[Public sector undertakings in India|Maharatna]] (PSU).<ref>{{Cite news|agency=Press Trust of India|date=2019-10-23|title=Govt accords 'Maharatna' status to Hindustan Petroleum, Power Grid Corp|work=Business Standard India|url=https://www.business-standard.com/article/pti-stories/govt-accords-maharatna-status-to-hindustan-petroleum-power-grid-corp-119102301347_1.html|access-date=2020-08-02}}</ref>

==History==
[[File:HPCL from Yarada hill.jpg|thumb|A view of HPCL from Yarada Hill, [[Visakhapatnam]]]]

HPCL was incorporated on 5 July 1952 as Standard Vacuum Refining Company of India Limited. In 1974, it changed its name to Caltex Oil Refining India Ltd. after the takeover and merger of erstwhile Esso Standard and Lube India Limited by the [https://indiankanoon.org/doc/1769128/ Esso (Acquisition of Undertakings in India) Act 1974]. Caltex Oil Refining (India) Ltd. (CORIL) was taken over by the Government of India in 1976 and merged with HPCL in 1978 by the [https://web.archive.org/web/20161031150739/http://www.hindustanpetroleum.com/Upload/En/UPdf/CORIL-AMALGAMATION-1978.pdf CORIL-HPCL Amalgamation Order 1978]. Kosan Gas Company was merged with HPCL in 1979 by the [https://web.archive.org/web/20161031024157/http://www.hindustanpetroleum.com/Upload/En/UPdf/KOSANGAS-ACQUISITION-ACT.pdf Kosangas Company Acquisition Act 1979].

In 2003, following a petition by the [[Centre for Public Interest Litigation]] (CPIL), the [[Supreme Court of India]] restrained the central government from privatizing Hindustan Petroleum and [[Bharat Petroleum]] without the approval of Parliament. As counsel for the CPIL, [[Rajinder Sachar]] and [[Prashant Bhushan]] said that the only way to disinvest in the companies would be to repeal or amend the Acts by which they were nationalized in the 1970s. As a result, the government would need a majority in both houses to push through any [[privatization]].<ref>{{cite book
 |url=https://books.google.com/books?id=ZBuUNzIgJjAC&pg=PA136 |page=136
 |title=Privatization and Labor Restructuring
 |author=Gopal Ganesh
 |publisher=Academic Foundation |year=2008 |isbn=978-8171886340}}</ref>

On 19 July 2017, the [[Government of India]] announced the acquisition of HPCL by the [[Oil and Natural Gas Corporation]] (ONGC).<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.hindustantimes.com/business-news/cabinet-allows-ongc-to-buy-out-govt-stake-in-refiner-hpcl/story-2oqzKRbSfScBDmCt3oiL2L.html|title=Cabinet allows ONGC to buy out govt stake in refiner HPCL|date=19 July 2017|website=hindustantimes.com|access-date=7 April 2018|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180212201943/https://www.hindustantimes.com/business-news/cabinet-allows-ongc-to-buy-out-govt-stake-in-refiner-hpcl/story-2oqzKRbSfScBDmCt3oiL2L.html|archive-date=12 February 2018|url-status=live}}</ref>
On 1 November 2017, the Union Cabinet approved ONGC for acquiring a majority 51.11% stake in HPCL. On 30 January 2018, ONGC acquired 51.11% stake, thus gaining majority ownership.<ref name="economictimes.indiatimes.com2"/>

==Operations==
[[File:Hindustan_Petroleum_Fueling_Station_Kapsi.jpg|thumb|An HP fueling station in [[Kapsi]], [[Chhattisgarh]]]]
[[File:Hindustan Petroleum Fuel Pump.JPG|thumb|HP fuel pump in [[Coimbatore]]]]
[[File:Hp basaveshwaranagar.png|thumb|HP petrol bunk at [[Basaveshwaranagara]], [[Bangalore]]]]

HPCL wholly owns two major refineries in India:<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.indiaprwire.com/pressrelease/information-technology/2010051750909.pdf |title=Hindustan Petroleum Corporation Limited Relies on Oracle Database Security Solutions |publisher=/www.indiaprwire.com |access-date=2010-07-26 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20130926215420/http://www.indiaprwire.com/pressrelease/information-technology/2010051750909.pdf |archive-date=26 September 2013 |url-status=dead }}</ref> one in [[Mumbai]] (west coast) with a capacity of 9.5 million [[ton]]s per year, and one in [[Visakhapatnam]] (east coast) with a capacity of 13.7 million tons per year.<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www-03.ibm.com/press/us/en/pressrelease/25041.wss |title=IBM News room - 2008-09-04 HPCL Partners With IBM to Deploy a Path-Breaking RFID Solution - United States |publisher=03.ibm.com |date=2008-09-04 |access-date=2012-11-09 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20111011134512/http://www-03.ibm.com/press/us/en/pressrelease/25041.wss |archive-date=11 October 2011 |url-status=dead }}</ref>

In addition, HPCL holds an equity stake of 16.95% in [[Mangalore Refinery and Petrochemicals Limited]], a company that runs a refinery in [[Mangalore]] with a capacity over 9 million tons per year. HMEL, a joint venture between HPCL and Mittal Energy Investments Pte. Ltd, operates another refinery of 11.3 million tons per year in [[Bathinda]], [[Punjab, India|Punjab]].<ref>http://www.hmel.in {{Webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20130624042524/http://hmel.in/ |date=24 June 2013 }} HMEL</ref> HPCL has signed a memorandum of understanding with the Government of [[Rajasthan]] for constructing a [[refinery]] near [[Barmer, Rajasthan|Barmer]]; it would be operated under a [[joint venture]] company called HPCL Rajasthan Refinery Limited (Popularly known as HRRL).<ref name="bp">{{cite web|title=HPCL to set up new Refinery in Barmer Rajasthan|url=http://news.biharprabha.com/2013/09/hpcl-to-set-up-new-refinery-in-barmer-rajasthan/|access-date=22 September 2013|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20131017061957/http://news.biharprabha.com/2013/09/hpcl-to-set-up-new-refinery-in-barmer-rajasthan/|archive-date=17 October 2013|url-status=live}}</ref>

HPCL also owns and operates the largest [[lubricant]] refinery in India, with a capacity of 335,000 metric tons, producing lube base oils.{{Citation needed|date=January 2023}} This refinery accounts for over 40% of India's total lube base oil production. HPCL produces over 300 grades of lubes, specialties, and [[Grease (lubricant)|greases]].

The marketing network of HPCL consists of 19 zonal offices in major cities and 145 regional offices<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.topnews.in/buy-hpcl-target-rs-490-2265932 |title=Buy HPCL With Target Of Rs 490 | TopNews |publisher=Topnews.in |date=2010-05-07 |access-date=2010-07-26 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120406172035/http://www.topnews.in/buy-hpcl-target-rs-490-2265932 |archive-date=6 April 2012 |url-status=live }}</ref> facilitated by a supply and distribution infrastructure comprising terminals, aviation service facilities, [[liquefied petroleum gas]] bottling plants and distributors, lube filling plants and distributors, inland relay depots, and retail outlets (petrol pumps).

HPCL has an [[information technology]] infrastructure to support its core business. The [[data center]] is at [[HITEC City]] in [[Hyderabad]].

According to a 2025 Financial Times investigation, the Guru Gobind Singh Refinery received multiple shipments of Russian crude oil transported part of the way on tankers listed under US and EU sanctions, involving ship-to-ship transfers offshore in the Gulf of Oman. The article noted that there was no evidence indicating whether the refinery’s operators were aware of the sanctioned status of the vessels.<ref>{{cite web |date=29 October 2025 |title=Lakshmi Mittal's energy venture bought Russian oil transported on blacklisted ships |url=https://www.ft.com/content/52999650-6a10-4666-a5f7-a58c236bff62 |website=Financial Times}}</ref>

=== Facilities ===
[[File:Visakhapatnam oil refinary.jpg|thumb|HP oil refinery in [[Visakhapatnam]]]]
HPCL operates refineries in India, including:
* [[Mumbai Refinery (HPCL)|Mumbai Refinery]]: 9.8 [[1,000,000|million]] [[Metric system|metric]] [[ton]]s capacity (fuel and lubes)
* [[Visakhapatnam Refinery]]: 15 [[million]] [[Metric system|metric]] [[ton]]s capacity (fuel)
* [[Mangalore Refinery and Petrochemicals Limited|Mangalore Refinery]]: 9.69 [[1,000,000|million]] [[Metric system|metric]] [[ton]]s capacity (HPCL has a 16.65% stake)<ref>{{cite web |title=Welcome to Mangalore Refinery and Petrochemicals Ltd |url=http://www.mrpl.co.in/ |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20191021081220/https://www.mrpl.co.in/ |archive-date=21 October 2019 |access-date=28 June 2013}}</ref>
* [[Guru Gobind Singh Refinery]] ([[Bathinda]]): 9 [[1,000,000|million]] [[Metric system|metric]] [[ton]]s capacity (HPCL and Mittal Energy each have a 49% stake)<ref>{{cite web |title=Home - HMEL |url=http://www.hmel.in/ |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150703002949/http://www.hmel.in/ |archive-date=3 July 2015 |access-date=2 July 2015}}</ref>
* [[Barmer Refinery]]: 9 [[1,000,000|million]] [[Metric system|metric]] [[ton]]s capacity (HPCL has a 74%, [[Government of Rajasthan]] has a 24% stake)<ref name="bp" />

In addition, HPCL operates other manufacturing facilities, including:

* Silvassa Lube: an automated installation and plant for grease and specialties
* Lube & Grease manufacturing facility ([[Mazagaon]], Mumbai)
* LPG storage Cavern: a storage facility of LPG at Vizag—SALPG<ref>{{cite web |title=SALPG - South Asia LPG Company Pvt Ltd |url=http://www.salpg.com/ |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150503005823/http://www.salpg.com/ |archive-date=3 May 2015 |access-date=2 July 2015}}</ref>
* Pipelines: MPSPL, MDPL, VVSPL, MHMSPL, RKPL, ASPL, RBPL
* Several terminals and depots{{Which?|date=January 2023}}
* Many{{How many?|date=January 2023}} liquified petroleum gas bottling plants
* HPCL Green R&D Centre ([[Bangalore]])

==Products==
[[File:HP Petrol Bunk 31102016.jpg|thumb|HP petrol pump]]
[[File:Tata ACE - HP Gas Carrier.JPG|thumb|HP cooking gas delivery vehicle]]HPCL produces a wide variety of petroleum fuels and specialties:
* [[Gasoline|Petrol]] (known as "motor spirit" in the oil industry) – HPCL markets its petrol at its retail pumps all over India. Its principal consumers are personal vehicle owners.
* [[Diesel fuel|Diesel]] (known as "high-speed diesel" in the oil industry) – HPCL markets its diesel at its retail pumps, terminals, and depots. Its consumers include personal vehicle owners, transport agencies, and industries.
* [[Lubricant|Lubricants]] – HPCL is the market leader in lubricants and associated products. It commands over 30% of the market share in this sector. The popular brands of HP lubes are Laal Ghoda, HP Milcy,<ref>{{Cite web |url=http://hpmilcy.com/ |title=:: Hp Lubes :: |access-date=6 December 2019 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120529225052/http://www.hpmilcy.com/ |archive-date=29 May 2012 |url-status=dead }}</ref> Thanda Raja, Koolgard, and Racer4.<ref>http://www.hpracer4.com/ {{Webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110208104222/http://hpracer4.com/ |date=8 February 2011 }} Racer4</ref>
* [[Liquefied petroleum gas]] – HPCL's brand of liquified petroleum gas is popular across India for domestic and industrial uses.
* [[Aviation fuel]]<ref>http://www.hpaviation.in {{Webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190423062242/http://www.hpaviation.in/ |date=23 April 2019 }} HP Aviation</ref> – With major air service facilities in all major airports of India, HPCL is a key player in this sector, supplying turbine fuel to major airlines. It also supplies fuel to the US.{{Citation needed|date=January 2023}}
* [[Emulsion]]s – HPCL manufactures [[White spirit]] oil.
HPCL also offers HP Drive Track Plus cards for consumers purchasing their products, and provides cashback as per the government cashback offers.

==International rankings==
* HPCL is a [[Fortune Global 500|''Fortune'' Global 500]] company and was ranked at position 259 in 2013. In 2016, HPCL was ranked 367.
* HPCL was featured on the [[Forbes Global 2000|''Forbes'' Global 2000]] list for 2013 at position 1217.
* HPCL was the 10th most valuable brand in India according to an annual survey conducted by Brand Finance and ''[[The Economic Times]]'' in 2010.<ref name="top10">{{cite web|title=India's top 10 brands|url=http://business.rediff.com/slide-show/2010/oct/26/slide-show-1-tata-motors-is-indias-top-brand.htm|publisher=business.rediff.com|access-date=26 Oct 2010|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20101028074814/http://business.rediff.com/slide-show/2010/oct/26/slide-show-1-tata-motors-is-indias-top-brand.htm|archive-date=28 October 2010|url-status=live}}</ref>

==Major ongoing projects==
* Uran–Chakan–[[Shikrapur, Maharashtra|Shikrapur]] LPG Pipeline (UCSPL)
* [[Vijayawada]]–Dharmapuri Pipeline (VDPL)
* Palanpur Vadodara Pipeline (PVPL)
* [[Visakhapatnam Refinery]] Modernization Project
*[[Mumbai Refinery]] Expansion Project

==Subsidiaries==

'''Hindustan Petroleum Gas'''

HPCL is focused on the appraisal and development of [[hydrocarbon]] accumulations in onshore and offshore projects. Operating projects include the Hirapur Marginal [[Petroleum reservoir|oil fields]] of the [[Cambay State|Cambay]] basin (near [[Gandhinagar]], Gujarat) under a service contract with ONGC, and the pre-NELP production sharing contract for the Sanganpur field ([[Mehsana district|Mehsana]]) with M/s Hydrocarbon Development Company (P) Ltd.
* HPCL Biofuels Limited
* CREDA-HPCL Biofuels Limited
* HP Gas (domestic and industrial natural gas)
* HPCL LNG Limited

extract:
Hindustan Petroleum Corporation Limited (HPCL) is an Indian public sector undertaking in petroleum and natural gas industry, headquartered in Mumbai. It is a subsidiary of the Oil and Natural Gas Corporation (ONGC), which is owned by the Government of India and under the administration of Ministry of Petroleum and Natural Gas.
Since 2018, Oil and Natural Gas Corporation has owned majority of its stake. It is ranked 367th on the Fortune Global 500 list of the world's biggest corporations as of 2016. On 24 October 2019, it became a Maharatna (PSU).
